free_tier.stated: Free tier, while HCP Vault Secrets was on sale: 25 static secrets, 25 applications, 5 versions per secret, 5 secret sync destinations and Bronze support. New customers lost access at end of sale on 2025-06-30, and applications were deleted at end of life on 2026-07-01.
free_tier.notes: The headline unit counted is the static secret. The Essentials and Standard tiers raised the caps to 2500 and 25000 secrets, but the product is now decommissioned.

retention.stated: 5 versions per secret on the Free tier; a deleted application's audit logs were not retained in the UI log viewer
retention.notes: Retention is by version count, not by a number of days.

egress.terms: unverified: no egress quota or per-GB price is stated on the pages read; secret values were read back through the REST API, whose rate limits were stated for the Essentials and Standard tiers only

interface_detail: A REST API with operations such as OpenAppSecrets and ListOpenAppSecretVersions, and a CLI run command that injects secret names containing an underscore into environment variables. The HCP web UI was the management console.
tooling: The HCP CLI vault-secrets commands, the HCP REST API and the HCP Terraform provider
chaining: A hosted secret store for API keys and credentials, with sync to third-party destinations and an HCP CLI run command for injecting secrets into application environments.

limits.value: 25 static secrets on the Free tier
5120 characters per secret value, on all tiers
5 secret versions per secret on the Free tier
5 secret sync destinations on the Free tier

limits_note: Auto-rotating and dynamic secrets were Standard tier only, so the Free tier had no rotation. The 6000 secret access and 2000 other API requests per minute limits were stated for the Essentials and Standard tiers only. Resource ceilings of 100 apps and 100 integrations per project, 300 secrets, 10 dynamic secrets and 15 syncs per app applied to all tiers.
binding_note: The 25-static-secret cap filled first on the Free tier, before the 25-application cap or the per-secret value size was reached.

identity_cost.detail: An HCP account was created with email and password, GitHub or IBMid. The create-account page says 'Visit the HCP portal and provide your email and a password.' A credit card was not asked for at signup: HCP started in a trial state with 500 USD in trial credits, and the billing page only recommends a card 'to ensure continuity of service when trial credits are depleted.' The signup page itself answered HTTP 503, so the exact form fields are unverified: behind a sign-up. The offer is now closed to new customers.

reliability_note: The offer was decommissioned by the vendor: end of sale on 2025-06-30, applications deleted at end of life on 2026-07-01. A known API bug disconnected all sync integrations from an app when an edit omitted the sync_integrations field; a deleted application's audit logs were not retained in the UI log viewer.
confidence_note: All numbers come from first-party pages: the IBM end-of-life notice and the archived HashiCorp tiers, constraints, account and billing documentation. The signup form fields are unverified behind a sign-up, and the signup page answered HTTP 503.

notes: HCP Vault Secrets was a hosted, multi-tenant secret store, not self-hosted software. Its free allowance was 25 static secrets. The product reached end of sale on 2025-06-30 and end of life on 2026-07-01, so it is dead as of the verification date. The live documentation URLs now redirect to HCP Vault Dedicated documentation; the original first-party text was read from the Wayback archive of the same HashiCorp developer URLs.
